fact: A natural-gas crater in Turkmenistan that's been burning since 1971, when Soviet engineers set it alight expecting it to burn out in weeks.
title: The Door to Hell

fact: The world's largest salt flat. In the rainy season a thin sheet of water turns 4,000 square miles of Bolivia into a perfect mirror.
title: Salar de Uyuni

fact: About 40,000 interlocking basalt columns, formed by a volcanic fissure ~60 million years ago. Legend says a giant built it as a stepping-stone to Scotland.
title: Giant's Causeway

fact: 200 miles of tunnels under Paris hold the remains of more than 6 million people, stacked wall-to-wall in the late 1700s to empty overflowing cemeteries.
title: Catacombs of Paris

fact: Barcelona's famous basilica has been under construction since 1882 — longer than the pyramids took to build. Gaudí knew he'd never see it finished.
title: Sagrada Família

fact: A small Czech chapel decorated with the bones of 40,000–70,000 people — including a chandelier made from nearly every bone in the human body.
title: Sedlec Ossuary

fact: The deepest known point on Earth: ~10,935 meters. Drop Mount Everest in here and its peak would still be 2 km underwater.
title: Challenger Deep

fact: One of the hottest, lowest places on Earth. Its sulfur springs and salt formations look so alien that scientists study it as a stand-in for Mars.
title: Danakil Depression

fact: Namibia's red dunes rise 300+ meters — among the tallest on Earth. At nearby Deadvlei, 900-year-old dead trees stand in cracked white clay.
title: Sossusvlei Dunes

fact: 3,000 quartzite-sandstone pillars towering over the forest — the floating mountains of Avatar were modeled on these.
title: Zhangjiajie Pillars

fact: A Yemeni island where a third of the plants grow nowhere else — including dragon blood trees that bleed red sap. Often called the most alien place on Earth.
title: Socotra

fact: An accident: a 1964 well drilled for irrigation hit geothermal water, was never capped, and grew into a rainbow-colored erupting geyser cone.
title: Fly Geyser

fact: Every last Tuesday of January, the town of Lerwick burns a full-size Viking longship in the world's largest fire festival — a tradition since the 1880s.
title: Up Helly Aa

fact: Buried by Vesuvius in 79 AD mid-day: bread still in ovens, graffiti on walls, election posters painted fresh. A Roman city frozen at lunch.
title: Pompeii

fact: In July 1947 something crashed on a ranch outside Roswell. The Army announced a 'flying disc', retracted it the next day — and UFO culture was born.
title: Roswell Incident Site

fact: 17,000-year-old paintings of bulls and horses, found by four teenagers and their dog in 1940. The original is sealed; visitors tour a replica.
title: Lascaux Caves

fact: A 15th-century Inca citadel at 2,430m, never found by the Spanish. It stayed hidden until Hiram Bingham was led there by a local farmer in 1911.
title: Machu Picchu

fact: Population ~220 — and nearly all of them live in one 14-story building, Begich Towers, which also holds the school, church, and police station.
title: Whittier, Alaska

fact: America's only incorporated town with a population of 1. Elsie Eiler is the mayor, clerk, treasurer, librarian — and runs the town's only bar.
title: Monowi, Nebraska

fact: A coal-mine fire has burned under this town since 1962. Almost everyone left; steam still rises from cracked streets. It inspired Silent Hill.
title: Centralia, Pennsylvania

fact: The world's northernmost town of size. Burials are banned — the permafrost won't decompose bodies — and leaving town requires a rifle for polar bears.
title: Longyearbyen, Svalbard

fact: An opal-mining town (pop. ~1,700) where most people live underground in old mine shafts to escape 120°F heat. Founded 1915 after a teenager found opal.
title: Coober Pedy

fact: Morocco's 'Blue City', washed in blue since the 1930s. Founded 1471 as a mountain fortress against the Portuguese.
title: Chefchaouen

fact: A Dutch village with no roads — only canals. Founded around 1230 by peat harvesters; residents still get around by whisper-quiet electric boats.
title: Giethoorn

fact: Pop. ~780, with 7,000 years of salt mining — the oldest known. So pretty that China built a full-size replica of the entire village.
title: Hallstatt

fact: 828 meters — the tallest building ever built. Its spire alone would be one of the tallest skyscrapers in most countries.
title: Burj Khalifa

fact: 979 meters — the tallest waterfall on Earth. The water falls so far it turns to mist before reaching the ground.
title: Angel Falls

fact: The coldest permanently inhabited place on Earth: −71.2°C recorded in 1924. Cars are left running all day or they won't restart.
title: Oymyakon

fact: One male aspen that cloned itself into 47,000 trees weighing 6,000 tons — the largest and possibly oldest (80,000 years) living organism on Earth.
title: Pando
